description.p: RingoMusic is a native GNOME music player for Apple Music. Use it to browse your library, search the catalog, and play songs, albums, and playlists.
You must have an Apple Music subscription to use this application.
The audio quality is AAC 256 kbps.
RingoMusic is not affiliated with Apple Inc. Apple Music is a trademark of Apple Inc.
This release makes the mini player less intrusive.

ul.li: The mini player shows the hint about how to keep it above other windows only the first two times it opens after the start.
An automatic check makes sure that the two lists of permitted library changes stay the same.

description.p: This release adds a mini player. It also makes favorites and ratings follow Apple Music more closely, and it uses only the functions that Apple documents.

ul.li: A mini player opens when you close the window and playback continues in the background. It shows the cover and the seek bar. The player controls appear when you point at the cover. Drag the cover to move it, and right-click the cover to keep it above other windows. To turn it off, use Preferences.
The "Dislike" menu item is now "Suggest Less", as in the Apple Music app.
After each change, the star and "Suggest Less" show the state that Apple Music confirms. If Apple Music does not confirm the change, a message tells you.
To remove an artist from your favorites, use the Apple Music app or music.apple.com. RingoMusic used a function that Apple does not document for this, and it also marked the artist as disliked.
The message about library functions shows one more time, with the updated list.
Stricter checks of the requests that change your library.
Less work during playback with a long queue: the progress updates no longer copy the queue.

description.p: This release adds library management: create playlists, add songs to playlists and to your library, and mark favorites and dislikes.

ul.li: Create playlists in your library.
Add songs and albums to your playlists.
Add songs, albums, and playlists to your library.

Add songs, albums, artists, and playlists to your favorites, and remove them again, with the star button. In a song list, the star shows before the duration: always for a favorite song, and when the pointer is over the row for other songs.
Dislike songs. A disliked song shows dimmed in song lists, also after a restart.
A message tells which library functions are only available in Apple's apps. The Account page in Preferences shows it again.
The New page has a calendar icon, so it no longer looks like the favorites star.
Fix: after a restart, the album and artist buttons of the player bar did not open their pages until a new song played.
A volume or position drag during a slow queue change gives only one change to the player, not one for each step of the slider.
Fix: a quit while the player page was still loading showed a JavaScript error dialog.

description.p: This release adds the New page, the Made For You page, and a richer artist page. It also makes the player more stable.

ul.li: New page: see the latest releases from Apple Music.
Made For You page in the library: your personal mixes from Apple Music.

The Artists page in the library shows the artist list and, next to it, the albums in your library of the selected artist. The Open Artist Page button over the albums opens the full artist page. In a narrow window, the list and the albums show one at a time.
The buttons of the app have rounded corners and no longer have the pill shape.

The artist page shows the latest release, the albums, the singles and EPs, the live albums, the compilations, the playlists, the albums the artist appears on, and similar artists, like in Apple Music. Each list scrolls sideways, and lists without items are hidden.
The artist page shows the genre, the origin, and the start year under the name. The Info button opens all the information about the artist, with the biography.
The artist page and its information take a tint from the artist photo.
On the artist page, each list with more items has a small Show More button at the right of its title.
A playlist description shows in one line. When it is longer, a small Show More button opens all of it.
A long album or playlist title wraps next to the artwork. The text moves under the artwork only in a narrow window.
Songs on the Search, New, and artist pages show in columns that scroll sideways, like in Apple Music.
The Search page can search your library: use the Apple Music and Library switch next to the search field.
On the Search page, each section with more results has a small Show More button at the right of its title. It opens a page with all the results of the section.
Fix: some albums and songs on the New page had no artwork.
Fix: artists in the library and in the library search had no photo.
Fix: on a slow start, the Widevine module and the session could go to the wrong folder, and autoplay could be blocked.
When Apple Music changes its web page in a way that RingoMusic cannot use, RingoMusic stops and shows a message. It does not restart the player again and again.
If the app and its player have different versions, RingoMusic tells you to install it again.
Fix: after a crash of the player, RingoMusic plays the song again from the position where it stopped. If the music was paused, it stays paused.
The window stays responsive while a queue change waits for the network.
The cache of Apple Music data saves new responses faster when it is large.
Artwork that shows in many places at the same time loads and decodes only once.
The filter of the library lists reacts faster in large libraries.
Fix: the animation was not smooth when an album opened from an artist page. The page color now changes after the animation.
The colors of the pages and of the player bar fade smoothly when they change.
Fix: closed album and artist pages stayed in memory.
The Flatpak package starts again. Versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 stopped at start because the settings schema was missing.
Sign-in is faster: the Apple ID dialog opens directly. You do not have to click the Sign In button on the site.
Sign in with your Apple ID and play your Apple Music library.
Search the catalog. Open songs, albums, and playlists.
Control the queue. Use media keys and the GNOME Shell controls.
The window adapts to narrow screens.
The application checks for a new release once a day. You can turn this off in the preferences.
The audio quality is AAC 256 kbps.
Only x86_64 is supported.
You need an Apple Music subscription.

description.p: First pre-release. It tests the release pipeline and the packages.

ul.li: The application checks for a new release once a day and shows a message with a link.
Turn the check off with the new "Check for updates" switch in the preferences.
